title: LLM Gateway vs API Gateway vs Reverse Proxy
summary: These three terms are related, but they have different primary responsibilities.
objectives: LLM Gateway vs API Gateway vs Reverse Proxy

sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
These three terms are related, but they have different primary responsibilities.

### A. API Gateway

An API Gateway is a centralized entry point for managing API traffic.

It commonly handles:

- Authentication.
- Authorization integration.
- Routing.
- Rate limiting.
- Request validation.
- Load balancing.
- API analytics.

Example: A company has customer, payment, order and inventory APIs. An API Gateway manages access to all these APIs.

### B. Reverse Proxy

A Reverse Proxy sits in front of backend servers and forwards client requests to them.

It commonly handles:

- Request forwarding.
- TLS termination.
- Load balancing.
- Connection management.
- Caching.
- Traffic distribution.

Example: Nginx receives an incoming HTTP request and forwards it to one of your FastAPI backend servers.

### C. LLM Gateway

An LLM Gateway manages AI-model-specific traffic and policies.

It can understand concepts such as:

- Model names and providers.
- Input and output tokens.
- Model parameters.
- Token-based quotas.
- Model routing.
- Provider-specific errors.
- LLM cost and usage.
- Streaming responses.

### Comparison table

| Feature | Reverse Proxy | API Gateway | LLM Gateway |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request forwarding | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| HTTP routing | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Authentication | Often | Yes | Yes |
| Rate limiting | Often | Yes | Yes |
| Model-aware routing | Not usually | Sometimes | Core capability |
| Token tracking | Not usually | Not usually | Common |
| LLM cost tracking | No | Not usually | Common |
| Provider abstraction | No | Not usually | Common |
| LLM-specific policies | No | Not usually | Common |
| Prompt/response controls | Not usually | Sometimes | May support |

### Architecture example

**Client / Frontend**

↓

**Reverse Proxy**

TLS · Traffic forwarding

↓

**API Gateway**

API authentication · General routing · API quotas

↓

**LLM Gateway**

Model routing · Token budgets · Provider abstraction

↓

**OpenAI**

**Claude**

**Gemini**

This is one possible architecture, not a mandatory three-layer design. Some products combine API Gateway and LLM Gateway responsibilities in one service. A reverse proxy may also be integrated into the same deployment.

**Interview point:** An LLM Gateway is model-aware. A traditional API Gateway primarily manages general API traffic. However, their features can overlap.
